testCases.input: Under the Insurance Contract Act, if a subsequent premium is not paid on time, what payment deadline can the insurer set for the policyholder?
testCases.actualOutput:
According to Section 38 of the Insurance Contract Act (VVG), if a subsequent premium is not paid in good time, the insurer may set the policyholder a payment deadline of at least two weeks. This notice must be provided in writing and at the policyholder's expense. Furthermore, the deadline must specify the individual amounts of the premium that are in arrears, as well as any interest and costs, and it must outline the legal consequences of not meeting this deadline.

If the insured event occurs after the deadline without the policyholder having paid the overdue amounts, the insurer is not obliged to make a payment. Additionally, the insurer may terminate the contract without prior notice if the policyholder has not settled the due amounts after the expiration of the deadline.

This information can be found on page 15 of the Insurance Contract Act (VVG).

testCases.input: What is the standard limitation period under the German Civil Code?
testCases.actualOutput:
The standard limitation period under the German Civil Code (BGB) is three years, as stated in Section 195. This period applies to most claims unless specified otherwise by law.

Source: englisch_bgb.pdf, page 30.
